note: THE PATTERN ITSELF -- `"${\\([^}]+\\)}"', character for character out of `s.el''s `s-lex-fmt|expand' -- because this is the one measured consumer of the contextual rule. Emacs answers (2 2 8 "abc"): the placeholder in "x ${abc} y" spans 2..8 and group 1 is the name inside the braces. kg answers (nil nil nil nil), which is why `s-lex-format' builds an EMPTY binding list and then raises. U.0 measured the other end of it: with the one pattern rewritten to a class kg's engine does read, `(let ((a 5)) (s-lex-format "${a}"))' answers "5" -- Emacs' answer -- so this item closes that want completely rather than advancing it.
